summary: Enterprise Suite AC-18 adds a review-only Postgres/RLS durable-storage schema foundation for later Oyatie cloud database integration. The plan validates tenant-scoped tables for policy admissions, group close rollups, cross-product Workflow plans, incident rollback plans, and ops commands; tenant/idempotency primary keys; required payload/audit evidence columns; ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; restrictive current_setting-based tenant policies; no-delete append-only semantics; and cloud-readiness-gate composition while keeping runtime database attachment, migration execution, live RLS verification, and durable storage readiness as non-claims.

findings: The crate is a small declarative storage plan and SQL renderer with no database connection, migration runner, or persistence side effect.
Validation requires tenant/idempotency keys, RLS enable+force flags, restrictive policy names, and no-delete append-only semantics.
The slice narrows broad durable-storage/Postgres-RLS blockers into a tested schema/RLS plan plus remaining runtime attachment and live verification blockers.
Cloud readiness remains false; the plan only adds reviewable pre-cloud persistence policy.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if tenant columns, idempotency scope, force RLS, no-delete policy, runtime overclaim guards, duplicate table detection, or rendered RLS SQL are weakened.
findings: Positive plan coverage and negative RLS/idempotency/runtime-overclaim paths are covered.
Developers can call enterprise_postgres_rls_storage_plan(), validate_enterprise_postgres_rls_storage_plan(), and render_enterprise_postgres_rls_migration() to inspect the durable-storage boundary.

Targeted Postgres/RLS storage check/test/clippy, cloud-readiness test/clippy, 38-package enterprise regression test/clippy, fmt, jq, data_class scan, quality-marker scan, dependency-seam gate, Oya VCS lifecycle, and audit-chain append-only checks are required for closeout.

alternatives_named: wire a live Postgres adapter now
extend the existing in-memory adapter with Postgres-shaped flags
add a review-only schema/RLS plan before runtime database attachment
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The schema/RLS plan makes tenant isolation, idempotency, and migration SQL reviewable before claiming live database behavior.
rejected_reasons: A live adapter would be premature without secrets, connection management, migration execution, and runtime RLS evidence.
Adding flags to the in-memory adapter would not validate table/RLS policy structure.

findings: The rendered SQL enables row-level security and forces RLS on all planned Enterprise Suite tables.
Restrictive policies bind USING and WITH CHECK to tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true).
The plan forbids BYPASSRLS-shaped identifiers, delete policy enablement, applied migration claims, and runtime DB attachment overclaims.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Validation checks five in-memory table specs and renders static SQL; no DB, network, cryptography, or hot request path exists.

findings.summary: The plan adds no runtime cost until a future adapter/migration slice attaches it.

findings: All new public struct fields in changed source carry data_class annotations.

The design follows official PostgreSQL row security guidance by requiring row-level security enablement, FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE POLICY USING/WITH CHECK expressions, and session setting access via current_setting.
The change is additive: one crate, one catalog row, spec/task/evidence updates, and readiness-gate composition. No database, migration, credential, or external resource is created.
The readiness report now exposes postgres_rls_storage_plan_ready and evidence refs for later dashboards.
Runtime migration application, live RLS evidence, and runtime audit-chain emission remain explicit non-claims.
Enterprise Suite AC-18 records the staged migration boundary from in-memory storage seams to review-only Postgres/RLS schema plan and later live adapter/runtime verification.
AC-15 cloud-readiness blockers now distinguish storage/RLS runtime attachment from schema plan readiness.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A review-only Postgres/RLS plan improves cloud readiness only if it refuses to claim applied migrations, live RLS verification, durable storage, or cloud database attachment.
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Later storage work would need to infer tenant/RLS/idempotency requirements from prose and in-memory storage behavior rather than a typed schema plan.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: The existing in-memory store owns local test storage; a separate Postgres/RLS storage-plan crate preserves no-runtime-DB claims while establishing durable schema policy.

findings: This is the next cloud-integration step after auth runtime: persistence isolation and idempotency are now typed before a live database adapter is attached.
Names use postgres-rls-storage-plan/foundation vocabulary and avoid durable adapter or live database readiness claims.
Enterprise Suite spec, plan, task list, catalog, multispectrum evidence, VCS evidence, and audit-chain references are part of the closeout set.
The crate sits under microservices/enterprise-suite/crates with a storage-governance catalog row and no new external database adapter layer.
No listener, route-handler mutation, durable store adapter, SQL client, migration runner, provider SDK, Workflow engine/broker, statutory rail, or runtime audit emitter was introduced.
The new Postgres/RLS storage-plan crate has no third-party dependencies; the readiness gate adds only a local workspace dependency on it.
No external wire API schema changes; the addition is a Rust control-plane/storage-plan struct set plus Enterprise Suite AC-18 metadata.
Validation and SQL rendering are deterministic checks over five fixed table plans with no clock, randomness, I/O, network, or database calls.
